name: Addressing, Routing and Switching
summary: The heart of the network: dividing addresses, choosing paths and wiring the equipment that gets the packet there.
prerequisites: Requires networks: addressing is where the previous course’s theory becomes configuration.
syllabus: Network equipment and what each device is for
IPv4 and IPv6 addressing in practice
topics: Equipment: router, switch, hub, modem, access point, firewall and load balancer
Network card, repeater, bridge and gateway
Topologies: bus, star, ring, mesh and hybrid
LAN, WAN, MAN, VLAN and VPN: where each one shows up
Client-server and peer to peer (P2P)
Design principles: hierarchy, redundancy, scalability and documentation
Simulators: Cisco Packet Tracer, GNS3, EVE-NG and Mininet
IPv4: classes, public and private addresses, loopback and broadcast
IPv6: notation, link-local addresses and why migration matters
Static and dynamic assignment: DHCP, scopes and reservations
NAT and PAT: how the internal network reaches the internet
Subnet masks, CIDR and calculating hosts per range
VLSM and efficient division of address blocks
Routing table, default gateway and metrics
Static routing: when it is still the right answer
Interior routing protocols: RIP, OSPF and EIGRP
Routing between autonomous systems: BGP
Switching: MAC table, collision and broadcast domains
VLANs, 802.1Q tagging and trunking
Spanning Tree Protocol and loop prevention
Link aggregation (LACP) and Power over Ethernet (PoE)
Inter-VLAN routing and layer 3 switches
